purpose: Definitions for conceptual tree children that are not separate empirical nodes. These records prevent the canonical tree from pointing into an undefined vocabulary while keeping project-defined concepts distinct from observed entities.
epistemic_rule: These are architecture/interpretation records unless explicitly linked to an empirical source elsewhere.

records.name: Origin
records.definition: The conceptual beginning or originating condition from which a sequence is described.

records.name: Creation
records.definition: The transition from an unmanifest or prior condition into an identifiable form or world.

records.name: Father–Son relationship
records.definition: The project relationship between source/father imagery and son/transformation imagery.

records.name: Heaven–Earth
records.definition: A symbolic vertical distinction between transcendent/source space and manifested/material space.

records.name: Spirit–Matter
records.definition: A project-defined distinction between immaterial meaning and physical embodiment.

records.name: Life–Death
records.definition: The boundary between living continuity and mortality, loss or transformation.

records.name: Above–Below
records.definition: A directional contrast used to represent elevation, hierarchy, descent and grounding.

records.name: Light–Darkness
records.definition: A symbolic contrast between visibility, illumination and concealment or uncertainty.

records.name: Identity–Non-identity
records.definition: The question of what makes an entity the same, different or continuous through change.

records.name: Distance
records.definition: Separation between nodes measured physically, institutionally, conceptually or temporally.

records.name: Belief Space
records.definition: A conceptual space in which beliefs can be compared by claims, practices, institutions and relationships.

records.name: Religious Cube
records.definition: A project visualization for examining religious concepts across multiple dimensions rather than a single linear scale.

records.name: Levels
records.definition: Ordered stages or positions in a framework; ordering does not by itself imply human worth.

records.name: Spine
records.definition: A central structural axis used to organize connected levels or branches.

records.name: Ascent
records.definition: Movement toward a higher or more integrated position within the project's symbolic architecture.

records.name: Descent
records.definition: Movement toward a lower, deeper or more materially grounded position.

records.name: Mountain
records.definition: Symbolic terrain for elevation, perspective, convergence and difficult ascent.

records.name: North Gate
records.definition: A symbolic entrance associated with the project's North orientation and transition into the Axis field.

records.name: Interface
records.definition: A boundary where two systems exchange information, matter, energy, authority or experience.

records.name: Experience
records.definition: The lived or observed state produced when a system is encountered from within a particular perspective.

records.name: Perception
records.definition: The process by which information is selected, organized and interpreted by an observer or system.

records.name: Passage
records.definition: A transition through a boundary from one state, location or condition to another.

records.name: Potato Boundary
records.definition: The physical or symbolic interface separating potato interior from its surrounding environment.

records.name: Potato Threshold
records.definition: A transition point in the Potato model where inside/outside, surface/interior or state changes become significant.

records.name: Son to Door
records.definition: A project-defined symbolic correspondence in which the Son is treated as a threshold or vessel between states.

records.name: Son to Ladder
records.definition: A project-defined correspondence connecting transformation of the Son with the Axis/Ladder structure.

records.name: Memory
records.definition: Retention of information or history that allows a system to preserve continuity across change.

records.name: Renewal
records.definition: Regeneration or reorganization that allows a system to continue after loss or transformation.

records.name: Love
records.definition: A broad project vocabulary for attachment, care, connection and generative concern; empirical uses require specific definitions.

records.name: Light
records.definition: Symbolic illumination, visibility, knowledge or life-supporting energy; not a claim about a supernatural substance.

records.name: Connection
records.definition: A relation linking entities so that information, resources, authority, influence or meaning can pass between them.

records.name: Coupling
records.definition: The degree to which changes in one component are linked to changes in another.

records.name: Flow
records.definition: Movement of matter, energy, money, information, people, authority or meaning through a system.

records.name: Stagnation
records.definition: A condition in which movement, renewal or adaptation becomes persistently constrained.

records.name: False Structures
records.definition: Project vocabulary for structures that appear stable while depending on contradiction, concealment or unsupported assumptions.

records.name: Loss of Connection
records.definition: Breakdown of a relationship needed for coordination, support, information or continuity.

records.name: Return
records.definition: A transition back toward an earlier state, source, relationship or pattern after divergence.

records.name: Bottleneck
records.definition: A constrained component through which a disproportionately large share of system capacity or flow must pass.

records.name: Cycle
records.definition: A recurring sequence in which a later state feeds back into an earlier state.

records.name: Spatial Potato
records.definition: The Potato studied as a three-dimensional object with position, orientation, geometry, boundary and internal structure.

records.name: Potato Surface
records.definition: The external geometry and skin of a potato, including curvature, texture, eyes and boundary conditions.

records.name: Potato Interior
records.definition: The internal material volume of the tuber, including tissue, water, starch and structural gradients.

records.name: Potato Centre
records.definition: A reference region used to study radial distance, symmetry, sections and internal geometry.

records.name: Potato Axis
records.definition: A chosen coordinate direction through the potato used for measurement, orientation and comparison.

records.name: Potato Section
records.definition: A cross-section or cut through the tuber used to reveal internal geometry and material structure.

records.name: Potato Wedge
records.definition: A sector-shaped portion of the tuber used to study cutting, boundaries and geometric transformation.

records.name: Potato Topology
records.definition: Study of connectivity and boundary structure under transformations that do not depend on exact metric dimensions.

records.name: Potato Invariants
records.definition: Measured properties that remain stable under a specified transformation, such as rotation or scaling.

records.name: Potato Cross-scale
records.definition: Comparison of structural patterns from cells and tubers through plants, farms, food systems and wider networks.

records.name: Body
records.definition: Embodied biological structure considered as an object, organism and interface with an environment.

records.name: World
records.definition: The manifested field of people, organisms, places, institutions, systems, matter and relationships.

records.name: Absurdity
records.definition: A deliberate Potatoism vocabulary for humour, contradiction and perspective-breaking rather than an empirical category.

records.name: Political Cube
records.definition: A multidimensional political visualization used to compare positions without reducing politics to one left/right axis.

records.name: Britain
records.definition: The British Isles/United Kingdom-related field as used by the North Programme; precise territorial scope is recorded per relationship.

records.name: One Economic Field
records.definition: The hypothesis that distinct jurisdictions can be studied as one interconnected economic system through observable flows and dependencies.

records.name: Many Nations
records.definition: The recognition that an integrated system can contain sovereign states with distinct laws, institutions and political authority.

records.name: Constitutions
records.definition: Foundational legal arrangements that allocate state authority, rights and institutional powers.

records.name: Public Finance
records.definition: Government revenue, expenditure, debt, assets, liabilities and fiscal institutions.

records.name: Industry
records.definition: Productive enterprises, industrial capacity, supply chains, labour and physical capital.

records.name: Research
records.definition: Organized production and evaluation of knowledge through scientific, technical, historical or other methods.

records.name: Labour
records.definition: Human work, skills, participation, employment, migration and the institutions surrounding work.

records.name: Repair
records.definition: A project term for interventions intended to restore function, resilience, connection or institutional capacity.

records.name: Dependency
records.definition: A condition in which one component relies on another for a necessary input, service, capability or outcome.
